title: How to make a trading bot with claude
author: farshadmomo
selftext:
I want to know what things should I know and what I should have an eye on while making the trading bot

And what gotcha's i should look out for

Everything i should know and what strategies I should use for building one

Thanks

comments.author: mdawe1
comments.body: Dont use the AI in the work flow use it to do research and code and manage back tests

comments.author: Common_Class
comments.body: Read some books or papers for starters

replies.author: farshadmomo
replies.body: The problem is every ai trading bot i have built doesn't get me any profit, the fee on each transaction cancels out the profits

replies.author: Poowatereater
replies.body: Exactly why the above user said read some books…..

comments.author: No_Bit_3377
comments.body: The hardest part is creating a trading strategy that will generate profit even manually. Automating it with AI is easy.

comments.author: DifficultyOwn3050
comments.body: build news agent where they fetch news from multiple sources via api, implement technical agents where they have indicators, fundamental agent, risk management agent, portfolio management agent, backtesting agent, or there are multiple open source projects they doing like kronos

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body: You can try my platform to see how it works. It is free and all the strategies are open and transparent. I'm adding support for Claude Code this week. Just check my Reddit posts.

comments.author: Horror_Office_5737
comments.body:
The way I have implemented AI into our product is not to invest. It’s to provide a better understanding on why a coin is in the position it’s in or if it’s something to stay away from, AI makes a lot of mistakes. If I could give u any advice it would be do not use AI to actually trade. Use it to provide the information to setup your trades.   
Some people will disagree with me, but I personally feel like AI should not be touching any of your actual money.

comments.author: OpeningArm2775
comments.body: look at this [post](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/comments/1ucu4og/i_spent_the_past_8_months_working_on_my_own/) from this sub you can use it as a foundation for any trading project you wanna create im not affiliated with the dude but its one of the most useful things ive seen someone opensource for free on reddit

comments.author: DV_Zero_One
comments.body: Would you expect AI to predict the results of every game in a weekend of sports fixtures?

comments.author: Ok-Draft2744
comments.body:
Do lots of paper trading yourself while building the bot so you know what this is about. Then build it with claude, backtest if you can and forward test (ie run live) with paper trading. Don't put money in it until it works consistently. 

From someone who lost from live trading with ai

comments.author: sonofbaker
comments.body: you have to be extremely specific with your prompts in a structured way for contextual purposes. You also must set rules and limits in [claude.md](http://claude.md) and don't let Claude run on its own freely. It has to follow your rules.
